text:
With seven minutes left in St. Paul, the Wild led 3-0 and the Avalanche, already without Nathan MacKinnon for the next 12 weeks, looked like a team waiting for the bus. Then Colorado scored three times, and Cale Makar won it in the fourth round of a shootout, 4-3. The Avalanche have won three straight.

Minnesota built the lead honestly at first. Joel Eriksson Ek scored at 7:49 of the first off Matt Boldy, Blake Coleman added a backhand at 12:36, and the Wild owned the period, 1.37 expected goals (the quality of chances, added up) to 0.60. Eriksson Ek's second, with 44 seconds left in the second period, was a 3% chance, and it felt like the dagger.

It wasn't. Devon Toews scored at 13:37 of the third with Mackenzie Blackwood pulled for an extra attacker, as NHL.com's Heather Rule noted. Artturi Lehkonen tipped in a Makar shot at 16:01. And with exactly a minute left, T.J. Hughes snapped in the tying goal from Lehkonen, a shot that moved Colorado's win chance from 6% to 48%. Hughes finished with a goal, an assist and six shots, and his 0.41 wins added led everyone. Colorado won the third 1.18 to 0.06 in expected goals. In the shootout the first seven shooters, Kirill Kaprizov and Boldy among them, were all stopped before Makar scored.

On the whole night, our replays of every shot favored Colorado 70% to 30%, and the Avalanche outattempted Minnesota 69 to 46. Jesper Wallstedt was solid, 28 saves on 31 shots and right at expected. Blackwood allowed about a goal more than his 22 shots deserved but made the biggest save of the night, on Maxim Shabanov in overtime. The Athletic's Michael Russo headlined his story with a Wild player's words: "Don't know what happened." For Minnesota, playing without a doubtful Quinn Hughes, it is the kind of collapse that will be replayed for a while. For Colorado, it is the kind of win that tells you a team missing its best player has not stopped believing it can take any game.
headline: Avalanche erase three-goal deficit, Makar ends it in shootout
